doan_van.noi_dung:
> **Remote Work and the Future of Cities**
> 
> For much of the twentieth century, the logic of urban growth was straightforward: firms clustered in city centres because proximity reduced the cost of doing business, and workers followed the jobs. This pattern held so consistently that planners rarely questioned it. The pandemic of 2020, however, forced a sudden and unplanned experiment. Millions of employees discovered that a substantial proportion of office work could be performed adequately from home.
> 
> The consequences have been uneven. In some cities, office occupancy has recovered almost entirely, while in others it remains well below pre-pandemic levels. Research conducted across twelve major cities suggests that the decisive factor is not the availability of technology, which is broadly similar everywhere, but the length of the average commute. Where commuting times exceeded roughly forty-five minutes, employees resisted returning; where journeys were shorter, most returned willingly.
> 
> This has produced a paradox. Remote work was expected to empty city centres and revive smaller towns. In practice, the towns that have gained most are those within commuting distance of large cities — places where residents can work from home for three days and travel in for two. Genuinely remote areas have benefited far less, largely because they lack the reliable infrastructure and services that hybrid workers still require.
> 
> Some economists argue that the long-term effect will be a redistribution rather than a reduction of urban activity. Offices may shrink, but the demand for housing, schools and transport in the surrounding region will grow. Others are more cautious, pointing out that firms have historically reversed such changes once competitive pressure returns. What is not disputed is that the assumptions guiding urban planning for the past fifty years can no longer be taken for granted.

**True / False / Not Given (46–51):**
46. Before 2020, urban planners frequently debated whether firms should cluster in city centres.
47. Office occupancy has recovered at similar rates across all cities studied.
48. The research covered more than ten cities.
49. Technology availability was found to be the main factor determining return-to-office rates.
50. Employees with commutes under forty-five minutes were more willing to return.
51. The research was funded by city governments.

**Điền từ (NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS) (52–55):**
52. Towns that have benefited most are located within ____________ of large cities.
53. Remote areas have gained less because they lack ____________ and services.
54. Some economists predict a ____________ of urban activity rather than a decline.
55. Cautious economists note that firms have previously ____________ such changes.

**Multiple choice (56–58):**
56. The main purpose of the passage is to:
A. argue that remote work will destroy cities
B. examine how remote work has affected urban patterns
C. advise firms on office policy
D. compare twelve cities in detail

1. The “paradox” mentioned refers to the fact that:
   A. technology was available everywhere
   B. offices reopened faster than expected
   C. nearby towns benefited more than genuinely remote ones
   D. commuting times increased after 2020
1. According to the final paragraph, economists agree that:
   A. offices will disappear
   B. urban activity will increase overall
   C. old planning assumptions are no longer reliable
   D. firms will reverse remote work policies

cau.en: Remote Work and the Future of Cities

pa.cau: Remote Work and the Future of Cities

- Kết bài 2 câu, không ý mới
- Kiểm tra: đọc riêng 4 câu đầu mỗi đoạn có ra dàn ý không?

**Part 1:** 8 câu về work, hometown, technology, free time.

- Lexical: dùng được ≥8 collocation chủ đề, có paraphrase khi lặp ý
- Grammar: ≥3 câu phức đúng, thì nhất quán
- Pronunciation: đuôi -s/-ed rõ, trọng âm từ đa âm tiết đúng, người nghe không phải đoán

# LỜI KẾT — SAU KHI HOÀN THÀNH 50 UNIT

Bạn đã đi hết bộ giáo trình: từ động từ “to be” ở Unit 1 đến đảo ngữ và mệnh đề rút gọn ở Unit 44.

**Ba việc nên làm tiếp:**

1. **Duy trì, đừng dừng.** Ngôn ngữ rơi nhanh hơn ta tưởng. Tối thiểu 30 phút/ngày: 1 bài đọc + 1 bài nghe + 10 phút nói.
1. **Chuyển sang nguồn thật.** Từ đây, thay giáo trình bằng The Economist, BBC, TED, podcast. Học tiếng Anh qua nội dung bạn thật sự quan tâm sẽ bền hơn học qua bài tập.
1. **Nếu mục tiêu là 7.0+**, thứ cần đầu tư không còn là ngữ pháp mà là **độ chính xác của từ vựng** (collocation, sắc thái) và **tư duy lập luận**. Ở ngưỡng đó, người chấm không hỏi “câu này có đúng ngữ pháp không” mà hỏi “người viết có nói được điều gì đáng nghe không”.

Chúc bạn thi tốt.
